question.text: Saffron Infrastructure Fund (Category II AIF) reports FY25: interest income INR 50 crore, LTCG on unlisted equity INR 30 crore, STCG on listed equity (STT-paid) INR 10 crore, and business income INR 5 crore. Ms. Meera Iyer, a resident individual LP, holds 4% of the units. What is Ms. Meera's pass-through share from the fund and what does the fund itself pay tax on?

answer.text: Meera receives INR 2 cr interest + INR 1.2 cr LTCG + INR 0.4 cr STCG + INR 0.2 cr business income, all taxed in her hands; fund pays nothing.
Fund pays tax on entire INR 95 cr at MMR and distributes post-tax; Meera reports nothing.
Meera receives only her pro-rata distribution net of 10% TDS; character doesn't pass through.
Meera's 4% share = INR 2 cr interest, INR 1.2 cr LTCG, INR 0.4 cr STCG (character retained) taxed in her hands; the fund pays tax on the INR 5 cr business income at MMR.

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 115UB, non-business income (interest 50 + LTCG 30 + STCG 10 = INR 90 cr) passes through in same character. Meera's 4% = INR 2 cr interest + INR 1.2 cr LTCG + INR 0.4 cr STCG, taxed in her hands at the head-wise rates (slab for interest; 12.5% for LTCG; 20% for STCG under Section 111A). Business income of INR 5 cr is taxed AT THE FUND at MMR (42.744%) under Section 10(23FBB) and is exempt in Meera's hands. Business income does NOT pass through. The Trap: Option A incorrectly passes business income through. Option B is the Cat III treatment, not Cat I/II. Option C ignores the statutory pass-through of character. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A distributor exam asks which heads flow through; XIX-C asks the manager to compute Form 64C entries per LP per head. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build the fund accounting system to tag every rupee of revenue by ITA head (interest, dividend, LTCG-listed, LTCG-unlisted, STCG, business) at source. This lets you auto-generate Form 64C/64D and prevent category leakage that the AO can re-characterise.
